I've been working this land for 20 years, so I know what works here in Quzhou. The soil is decent but rainfall is unreliable — good thing I have the well. My husband and eldest son work off-farm now, so I can't be too labor-heavy. I need crops that bring steady cash and don't bury me in work alone.

My main system stays wheat-maize. I put 3 mu into that rotation — wheat in autumn, maize right after harvest in June. It's what everyone does here and it pays reliably. I won't change what works. I keep 1 mu for cotton — the price has been okay and I know how to grow it, even though picking season is brutal. The last 1 mu goes to peanut. Peanut is easier on the soil, and I can sell it locally without depending on traders coming through.

For wheat I'll use an improved variety — the seed station near town has good stock. I do two irrigations: the winter freeze-in irrigation in November and one at jointing in April. I apply base fertilizer before planting and top-dress in spring. Rotary tillage after maize harvest, then sow.

For maize I go no-tillage, direct seeding into the wheat stubble. Hybrid seed, of course. I split my nitrogen — some at planting, more at the big bell stage. Two irrigations unless we get summer rain.

For cotton, I use hybrid Bt seed. That cuts down on bollworm spraying. But I still spray 4 times for aphids, spider mites, and fungal blight. Cotton needs 4 irrigations — it's thirsty. I plough this plot since cotton roots need room.

For peanut, I plough deep and ridge-plant. Peanut fixes its own nitrogen so I go light on N, heavier on phosphorus and potassium. Two irrigations, one herbicide pass, done.
